name: Learn: Scheduling
description: Master how pods land on nodes — node labels + nodeSelector, taints & tolerations, nodeAffinity, manual scheduling with nodeName, and running one pod per node with a DaemonSet.
objective: CKA › Workloads & Scheduling (15%). Goal: control where pods land — labels/nodeSelector, taints & tolerations, nodeAffinity, manual scheduling, and DaemonSets.

questions.title: Labels + nodeSelector
questions.teach:
The scheduler can be steered with **node labels**. A `nodeSelector` on a pod is the simplest constraint: the pod will **only** schedule onto a node whose labels contain **every** key/value in the selector (it is an AND of exact equalities — no operators, no ranges).

Label a node with `kubectl label node <node> <key>=<value>`, then put the same key/value under `spec.nodeSelector`.

**Ways to constrain where a pod lands (increasing power):**
- `nodeSelector` — exact label equality only; multiple entries = AND.
- `nodeName` — hard pin, bypasses the scheduler (step 4).
- `nodeAffinity` — operators `In/NotIn/Exists/Gt/Lt`, required vs preferred (step 3).
- `podAffinity`/`podAntiAffinity` — co-locate / spread relative to other pods via `topologyKey`.
- `topologySpreadConstraints` — even spread across zones/nodes (`maxSkew`, `whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule|ScheduleAnyway`).

**Useful built-in node labels** (no need to add your own): `kubernetes.io/hostname`, `kubernetes.io/os`, `kubernetes.io/arch`, `topology.kubernetes.io/zone`, `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane`.

**Gotchas:**
- No matching node → the pod stays `Pending` forever (check `kubectl describe pod` events / `kubectl get events`).
- Label keys/values that are selectors must match **exactly**; use `--overwrite` to change an existing label and `kubectl label node <node> key-` (trailing dash) to remove one.
- `nodeSelector` cannot express "not" / ranges / OR — reach for `nodeAffinity` when you need those.
- `nodeSelector` does **not** override a taint; a tainted target node still needs a matching toleration (step 2).
questions.prompt:
A worker node named like `$W1` exists. Label it `disktype=ssd`, then in namespace `sched-learn` create a pod `ssd-pod` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) with a `nodeSelector` of `disktype=ssd`.

Target: pod `ssd-pod` is `Running` and its `.spec.nodeName` equals the labeled node.
questions.hint: `kubectl label node "$W1" disktype=ssd`, then build the pod YAML with `spec.nodeSelector.disktype: ssd` (or `kubectl run ssd-pod --image=busybox:1.36 --overrides=... -- sleep 3600`).
questions.solution:
kubectl label node "$W1" disktype=ssd --overwrite
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ssd-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    disktype: ssd
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: ssd-pod is Running on the node labeled disktype=ssd

questions.title: Taints + tolerations
questions.teach:
A **taint** on a node repels pods that don't tolerate it — `kubectl taint node <node> key=value:NoSchedule`. A pod opts in by declaring a matching **toleration** under `spec.tolerations`.

Taints/tolerations only *allow* scheduling onto a tainted node; they don't *force* it there (that is affinity/nodeSelector's job). This is the opposite polarity from affinity: taints repel, affinity attracts.

**The three effects:**
- `NoSchedule` — new intolerant pods are rejected; existing pods stay.
- `PreferNoSchedule` — soft version; scheduler tries to avoid but may still place.
- `NoExecute` — intolerant pods are also **evicted**. With `tolerationSeconds: N` a tolerating pod stays only N seconds after the taint appears.

**Toleration matching:**
- `operator: Equal` (default) needs `key`, `value`, and `effect` to match.
- `operator: Exists` matches any value for the key; omit `value`.
- Empty `key` + `operator: Exists` tolerates **everything** (used by DaemonSets, step 5).
- Omitting `effect` tolerates **all effects** for that key.

**Gotchas:**
- A toleration is a license, not a magnet — pair it with `nodeSelector`/affinity to actually land on that node (as this step does).
- Remove a taint with a trailing dash: `kubectl taint node <node> key=value:NoSchedule-`.
- Well-known taints auto-applied by the system: `node.kubernetes.io/not-ready`, `.../unreachable` (NoExecute), and `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule` on control-plane nodes.
- `NoExecute` on an already-running pod with no toleration will evict it — watch for this in restore/upgrade scenarios.
questions.prompt:
Taint node `$W1` with `workload=batch:NoSchedule`. Then in `sched-learn` create pod `batch-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) that **tolerates** that taint AND uses a `nodeSelector`/affinity so it lands on `$W1`.

Target: `batch-pod` is `Running` on `$W1` (proving the toleration let it through the taint).
questions.hint: `kubectl taint node "$W1" workload=batch:NoSchedule`. Give the pod a toleration `{key: workload, value: batch, effect: NoSchedule}` plus `nodeSelector: {disktype: ssd}` (reuse step 1's label) so it targets $W1.
questions.solution:
kubectl taint node "$W1" workload=batch:NoSchedule --overwrite
kubectl label node "$W1" disktype=ssd --overwrite
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: batch-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    disktype: ssd
  tolerations:
  - key: workload
    operator: Equal
    value: batch
    effect: NoSchedule
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: node $W1 is tainted and batch-pod tolerates it and runs there

questions.title: nodeAffinity (requiredDuringScheduling)
questions.teach:
**nodeAffinity** is a richer nodeSelector, living under `spec.affinity.nodeAffinity` and matching node labels via `matchExpressions` (or `matchFields`). Operators: `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, `DoesNotExist`, `Gt`, `Lt` — far more expressive than plain equality.

**Two flavors:**
- `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` — **hard** rule. Uses `nodeSelectorTerms` (a list). If unsatisfiable the pod stays `Pending`.
- `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` — **soft** rule. A list of `{weight: 1-100, preference: {matchExpressions}}`; the scheduler scores nodes but will still place the pod somewhere if no preferred node exists.

**AND vs OR (the classic trap):**
- Multiple `matchExpressions` **inside one** `nodeSelectorTerms` entry = **AND**.
- Multiple `nodeSelectorTerms` entries (separate `- matchExpressions:` list items) = **OR**.

**Gotchas:**
- `IgnoredDuringExecution` means node labels changing *after* the pod is scheduled do **not** evict it — affinity is only enforced at scheduling time (unlike `NoExecute` taints).
- Required nodeAffinity and `nodeSelector` on the same pod are **both** applied (AND); don't let them conflict.
- Affinity does not defeat taints — a target node that is tainted still needs a toleration, which is why this step's pod also carries `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]`.
- Related: `podAffinity`/`podAntiAffinity` work the same way but match **pod** labels within a `topologyKey` domain, not node labels.
questions.prompt:
Node `$W1` is labeled `tier=gold`. In `sched-learn` create pod `affinity-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) using **required** nodeAffinity matching `tier In [gold]`.

Target: `affinity-pod` is `Running` on the node labeled `tier=gold`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: affinity-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - key: tier
            operator: In
            values: ["gold"]
  tolerations:
  - operator: Exists
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: affinity-pod is Running on the node labeled tier=gold

questions.title: Manual scheduling with nodeName
questions.teach:
Setting `spec.nodeName` directly **bypasses the scheduler** entirely — the kubelet on that exact node just picks the pod up and runs it. This is how you place a pod when the scheduler is down, or to pin it deterministically.

**What nodeName skips vs still enforces:**
- **Skipped** (these are scheduler checks): `NoSchedule`/`PreferNoSchedule` taints, `nodeSelector`, `nodeAffinity`, `podAffinity`, topology spread.
- **Still enforced by the kubelet**: resource fit (a pod too big for the node goes `OutOfcpu`/`OutOfmemory`, not `Pending`), and `NoExecute` taints still evict/reject it.

**Gotchas:**
- A bad/nonexistent node name does **not** error — the pod just sits `Pending` with no scheduler event, because no scheduler ever looked at it. Confusing in the exam; double-check the exact node name from `kubectl get nodes`.
- `nodeName` and a `nodeSelector`/affinity on the same pod: the scheduler is bypassed so the selector/affinity is effectively ignored — don't rely on them together.
- This is also what a static pod shows (nodeName set by the kubelet), and how DaemonSet pods used to be placed historically.
- Contrast with a **Binding** object: `kubectl` / API can bind an already-`Pending` pod to a node after the fact; `nodeName` sets it at creation.
questions.prompt:
In `sched-learn` create pod `manual-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) that is bound to worker node `$W2` **via `spec.nodeName`** (no nodeSelector/affinity).

Target: `manual-pod` is `Running` and `.spec.nodeName` == `$W2`.
questions.hint: Add `nodeName: <the $W2 node name>` at the top of `spec`. Find the name with `kubectl get nodes`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: manual-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  nodeName: $W2
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: manual-pod is Running and pinned to $W2 via nodeName

questions.title: DaemonSet (one pod per node)
questions.teach:
A **DaemonSet** ensures a copy of a pod runs on **every** (matching) node — used for log shippers, node agents, CNI, kube-proxy, etc. As nodes join/leave, the DaemonSet controller adds/removes pods automatically.

**Targeting a subset of nodes:** add a `spec.template.spec.nodeSelector` or `nodeAffinity` to the pod template — the DaemonSet then runs only on matching nodes (e.g. only GPU nodes).

**Required fields** (like a Deployment, minus `replicas`): `spec.selector.matchLabels` **must** match `spec.template.metadata.labels`, or the API rejects it.

**Update strategy** (`spec.updateStrategy.type`):
- `RollingUpdate` (default) with `maxUnavailable` (and, 1.22+, `maxSurge`).
- `OnDelete` — pods update only when you delete them manually.

**Gotchas:**
- Control-plane nodes carry `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule`, so a DaemonSet meant to cover *all* nodes needs a toleration — `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]` tolerates every taint (used here).
- The scheduler places DaemonSet pods using normal affinity/taint rules (via an injected `nodeAffinity` on `kubernetes.io/hostname`); a `NoSchedule` taint with no matching toleration means that node simply gets **no** pod, and `desiredNumberScheduled` won't include it.
- DaemonSets ignore `replicas`/manual scaling — count is driven by node count. Read status from `desiredNumberScheduled`, `currentNumberScheduled`, `numberReady`.
- No `nodeSelector`/affinity + broad toleration = a pod on literally every node, including control plane — exactly this task's target.
questions.prompt:
In `sched-learn` create a DaemonSet `node-agent` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`, label `app=node-agent`) with a toleration broad enough (`operator: Exists`) to run on **every** node including the control plane.

Target: the DaemonSet has one ready pod on each node — `desiredNumberScheduled` == number of nodes and `numberReady` matches.
questions.hint: DaemonSet selector `app=node-agent`, pod template tolerations `- operator: Exists`. Verify with `kubectl -n sched-learn get ds node-agent` and `kubectl get nodes`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: node-agent
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: node-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: node-agent
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - operator: Exists
      containers:
      - name: c
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: DaemonSet node-agent runs one ready pod on every node
